semantic_contract: Announce a keyed, tagged editor action to a process-wide sink. Invariants, in the order the code establishes them: (1) the function has no receiver, no stack frame locals and no memory writes; (2) its single argument is a 32-bit opaque tag identifying the action, forwarded unchanged; (3) it first reads one 32-bit context value from the sink, which is 0 when the sink is absent; (4) it then asks the sink to open a record under a fixed scope name, store the caller's tag under a fixed first key, store the context value under a fixed second key, and close the record - four virtual calls in that fixed order on slots +0x38, +0x40, +0x40 and +0x58 of the sink; (5) if the sink is absent, both halves are no-ops: the context read yields 0 and the emit is skipped entirely, so the function has no observable effect and no return value; (6) the two outgoing words are cleaned by this function with ADD ESP,8, so it is a plain cdecl free function; (7) the function is idempotent with respect to its own state - it reads nothing but the sink and the argument, and writes nothing at all; (8) because the scope name and the two keys are link-time addresses into a module that is not present in this installation, the record's externally visible payload cannot be read here, so the semantic content of the tag is not established.
classification_rationale: The complete 28-byte body, the cdecl ABI, the argument order across both callees, the four virtual slots and their fixed order, the three key constants and the whole no-op-when-absent behaviour are read directly from the disassembly, and the same sequence is independently corroborated by the compiler-generated inlined duplicate at 0x005def30 and by 19 callers that consistently place the call immediately before an editor state change, an undo or a redo. STRONG_SEMANTIC is withheld on two named bounds: the class behind DAT_0166D9F4 is not identified and no concrete callee was resolved for any of the five virtual slots, and the three key constants address string literals in a module absent from this installation so their text, and therefore the record's meaning, cannot be recovered. The 'announce an undo/redo transaction' reading is explicitly INFERRED, not asserted. STRUCTURAL_ONLY is not applicable: the behavioural claim is supported by the body, the inlined duplicate and the caller argument patterns, not by structure alone.
semantic_findings: The function is a two-line adapter: it turns one caller-supplied tag into a four-call sequence on a shared service, and it exists only because that sequence appears in 19 places across four editor front ends. The compiler inlined it once, at 0x005def30, which is why the duplication is invisible in the call graph.

The argument-to-key mapping is asymmetric and is fixed by the code: the caller's tag goes under key 0x03475381 while the sink's own +0x20 context value goes under key 0x03475385. The sibling 0x00435f40 stores a caller-supplied value under that same 0x03475385, so 0x03475385 names a property the record always carries and 0x03475381 names the action being announced.

The whole function is guarded by a single global. Both callees re-read DAT_0166D9F4 through the same one-instruction accessor and null-check it independently, so the target evaluates the accessor twice and can, in principle, emit a record with a zero context value if the singleton were installed between the two reads. No caller can observe that race and none is claimed.

The function performs no write of any kind, so it cannot be the mutator of anything it reports. Every inspected caller places it immediately before the actual mutation or before cEditor::Undo / cEditor::Redo, which is the signature of a notification or transaction-open rather than an action.

Its 19 callers span the Editor, Palettes, Sporepedia and ArgScript regions, and the single most frequent argument 0x00A03E74B2 appears in 6 of them. A tag that generic is consistent with a 'generic editor change' marker rather than a per-feature identifier.

The static image proves the singleton is null at rest (0x0166D9F4 reads as 0x00000000), so in the shipped binary as imported every call to this function is a no-op. That is a statement about the static image only; no runtime claim is made.
unresolved_questions: What class is behind DAT_0166D9F4? Its shape - slot +0x20 returning a context value, +0x38 taking a scope name, +0x3C/+0x40 taking key/value pairs, +0x58 closing, and +0xC4 as a no-argument update called from 0x00a228b0 - is observed, but no SDK header matches it and no vtable for it was located. Spore/App/IMessageManager.h was read and rejected: its +0x38 is ProcessQueue2() with no argument and its +0x40 is Lock(bool), which contradicts both observed shapes.

What do the strings at 0x03475365, 0x03475381 and 0x03475385 say? All three lie outside SporeApp.exe's image span and carry no base relocation, so they address literals in a sibling Spore module. 2661 dwords in this image's .rdata point into 0x02xxxxxx-0x05xxxxxx, which is consistent with Spore's modules sharing one fixed address map, but no such module is present in this installation and none of the installed PE files has a preferred base near 0x03470000.

Who installs the singleton? A raw byte scan of the whole .text for the four-byte pattern of 0x0166D9F4 finds exactly the 24 references Ghidra reports, and every one of the three observed writes stores zero. No instruction in SporeApp.exe ever stores a non-null value, so the installation must happen in another module of the same process.

Is the record an undo/redo transaction, a change notification, or a telemetry event? The call sites immediately preceding cEditor::Undo and cEditor::Redo make an undo/redo reading the most economical, but the +0x38 and +0x40 targets are unresolved, so this stays INFERRED.

Does the tag have a stable public meaning, or is it a per-build hash of a source identifier? Every inspected argument is an opaque 32-bit value with no accompanying string, and no decoding table was found.
What is slot +0x3C for? It appears only in the sibling 0x00435f40, never in this target's sequence, so the difference between the two records is not established.

Why does 0x00435ed0 open with PUSH ECX (0x00435ed3)? It reserves the four-byte local at [EBP-4] and the following CALL passes no argument, so it is not a thiscall receiver. This is stated so the decompiler's phantom __thiscall signature on 0x00435ed0 is not mistaken for evidence.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace has ever been captured for this function; the original Cell stage has never been entered in any recorded run. Every claim here is static.

A runtime differential test is required to (a) observe the singleton being installed, (b) capture the concrete implementations behind slots +0x20, +0x38, +0x40 and +0x58, and (c) read the three key strings out of the sibling module once that module is available. Without (a) the static observation that the function is a no-op in the imported image says nothing about the shipping build.
The undo/redo inference additionally requires observing a listener that reacts to the emitted record.
blockers: The three key/scope constants address a module that is not shipped in this installation, so the record payload cannot be read. This bounds the classification but does not block the body reconstruction.
